newsitem.title: VIETNAM: First U.S. ambassador to Vietnam arrives in Hanoi.
newsitem.headline: First U.S. ambassador to Vietnam arrives in Hanoi.

text.p: The United States' first ambassador to Hanoi, former Vietnam War fighter pilot and prisoner of war Douglas "Pete" Peterson, arrived on Friday to take up his post.

Peterson, who landed at Hanoi's Noi Bai airport on a Thai Airways flight from Bangkok, takes over from the charge d'affaires who has headed the U.S. embassy since the two countries normalised relations in July, 1995.
Vietnam's ambassador to the United States, career diplomat Le Van Bang, 50, was due to arrive in Washington at around the same time.
U.S. officials said Peterson would make a brief statement to reporters at the airport and then head either to the embassy or the residence of his predecessor, Charge d'Affaires Desaix Anderson.
Sixty-one-year-old Peterson, whose posting was long delayed by domestic politics and legal wrangling, arrived almost exactly 22 years after the communist victory over U.S.-backed forces in 1975.

Progress on bilateral ties since normalisation, especially on a trade deal, has been painstakingly slow. Washington says that accounting for servicemen still missing in action (MIA) from the war remains its priority and diplomats on both sides concede that mutual suspicions still need to be overcome.
